title: Ceres: Celestial Legend
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: On their sixteenth birthday, twins Aya and Aki learn their wealthy Mikage family descends from a celestial maiden (tennyo) trapped into marriage by a mortal man; Aya is her reincarnation and the family moves to kill her. Aya goes on the run while Aki is possessed by the Progenitor, the ancestor who seized the tennyo, and the Mikage Group pursues a plan to breed human-tennyo hybrids. Yuu Watase's shoujo melodrama mixes romance, action and myth.
life_message: A woman's life is her own: love freely chosen, not taken by force.

content.note: Gunfights, stabbings and blood (ANN); murders and attempted murder (MU categories).
A family hunts Aya; possession and a vengeful spirit; long menace scenes (ANN).

Repeated attempted rape by the Progenitor in her brother's body, an incest theme stated plainly by ANN; MU Attempted Rape; AniList Rape and Incest tags. Sex scenes between Aya and Toya obscured with flowers (ANN).

Violence and coercion are framed negatively (to verify).

folkways.japan: The tennyo (celestial maiden) legend is a Japanese folk tale; the wealthy clan's control over heirs reflects older ie (household) norms that the story critiques.

delivery.evidence: ANN says Watase 'lectures her readers' in author's notes on love and gender and finds the series 'sometimes too talky'.
delivery.note: The gender theme is stated openly in dialogue and author notes, while Ceres' own anger is also questioned.

winners_losers: Aya and her chosen love win sympathy; the patriarchal Progenitor and the eugenic Mikage Group are the losers. Ceres' vengeance is shown with ambivalence.
to_verify: Strawman call for the Progenitor rests on Watase's own words quoted by ANN; a second review would confirm
